source.title: Londonderry Sentinel, 31 May 1927, p. 3 ("A majority of nine"); Londonderry Standard, 30 May 1927, p. 9 ("Narrow majorities: secure seats on Derry local boards")
source.publisher: Londonderry Sentinel (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: votes as printed: 'Mr. J. C. Drennan, J.P. ... 505; Mr. William Loughrey ... 496', a majority of nine, with twenty-two spoiled votes and roughly 60 per cent of the electors voting (Londonderry Sentinel, 31 May 1927); the Londonderry Standard of 30 May prints the same figures

note: Nominations were received on 21 April 1927 and printed in the Belfast News-Letter of 22 April, with retiring members marked by an asterisk; withdrawals closed on 28 April (News-Letter, 29 April). Marcus Smyth and Wm. H. Reed withdrew in Faughanvale, leaving George Leeke returned unopposed, so Bellarena alone was contested, between Wm. Loughrey and J. C. Drennan, both Unionists. The poll was taken on Friday 27 May 1927 and the votes were counted on Saturday morning, 28 May, when Drennan was returned by 505 to 496 (Londonderry Sentinel, 31 May 1927). No nominations were received for Dungiven or Claudy, whose sitting members Patrick M'Closkey and Cyril A. Nicholson were treated as re-elected. Polled Friday 27 May 1927: 'Polling took place yesterday in the Bellarena division of county Londonderry, the only division in the county where there was a contest' (Londonderry Sentinel, Saturday 28 May 1927, p. 8). Re-filed from 1927-05-26 (gap-fill 6 Nov 2026), which had been inferred from the Saturday count. Both candidates were Unionists. The former member, John Morrison, J.P., did not seek re-election. The votes were counted on the morning of Saturday 28 May 1927; the poll was on Friday 27 May (Londonderry Sentinel, 28 May 1927, p. 8).
